Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 48, verse 15:

Explanation of the words:

"Those who were left behind among the Bedouins" (al-mukhallafun min al-a'rab): i.e., those mentioned in the verses before this one, namely Ghifar, Juhaynah, Muzaynah and Ashja'.

"When you set out to take spoils" (idha intalaqtum ila maghanima li-ta'khudhuha): i.e., the spoils of Khaybar, which God had promised them when they returned from al-Hudaybiyah.

"Let us follow you" (dharuna nattabi'kum): i.e., let us go out with you to obtain a share of the spoils.

"They want to change the word of God" (yuridduna an yubaddilu kalam Allah): i.e., by their request to go out to Khaybar to seize the spoils, they want to change God's promise to the people of al-Hudaybiyah, which was specifically of the spoils of Khaybar.

"Thus God said before" (kadhalikum qala Allah min qabl): i.e., He, exalted is He, said to us before our return to Madinah: you will not follow us, and you will not go out with us.

"They will say, 'No, you envy us'" (fa-sa-yaqulluna bal tahsudunana): i.e., they will say, "No, you envy us." And indeed they did say so, and they claimed that this prohibition was not a command from God but came from the Messenger and the believers out of envy toward them. This indicates their hypocrisy and disbelief, may God protect us.

"Rather, they understood but little" (bal kanu la yafqahuna illa qalilan): i.e., they do not understand with the understanding of the shrewd and skilled man except a little, and only in worldly matters.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues in seeking the guidance of the hypocrites, from the settled folk and the Bedouins, by speaking of them, uncovering their faults, and calling them to repentance and return to the truth when their deviation and evil conditions became apparent. 3- Removing sin and blame from staying behind from jihad for the excuse of blindness, lameness or illness.

4- Clarification of Allah's promise and threat to those who obey Him and those who disobey Him: the promise of Paradise and the threat of the Fire.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 48, verses 18–19**

**Explanation of the words:**

*"Indeed Allah was pleased with the believers"*: that is, those firm in faith and strong in it, who are the people of the Pledge of Ridwan (*Bay'at al-Ridwan*, the Pledge of Good Pleasure) from among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

*"When they pledged allegiance to you"*: that is, at al-Hudaybiyyah (a place near Makkah), O Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ).

*"Under the tree"*: that is, a samurah tree (a kind of acacia). They numbered one thousand four hundred, and they pledged to fight the Quraysh and not to flee.

*"He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them"*: that is, Allah knew what was in their hearts of truthfulness and loyalty, so He sent down calm and steadfastness in what they were upon.

*"And rewarded them with a near victory"*: that is, it was the conquest of Khaybar, after their return from al-Hudaybiyyah in Dhu al-Hijjah. At the end of Muharram of the seventh year (AH), they campaigned against Khaybar, and Allah the Exalted granted them its conquest.

*"And much booty that they will take"*: that is, from Khaybar.

*"And Allah is ever Exalted in Might, Wise"*: that is, Allah the Exalted was and still is Mighty, Dominant, and Wise in His management of the affairs of His servants.

**The meaning of the two verses:**

The words of the Exalted, *"Indeed Allah was pleased with the believers"*, are an announcement from Him, the Exalted, of His pleasure with the believers who were complete in their faith. They were one thousand four hundred who pledged allegiance to the Messenger (ﷺ) under the samurah tree, except al-Jadd ibn Qays al-Ansari, for he did not pledge. He was hiding, pressed against the belly of his camel, concealed from the eyes of the Companions. He was a hypocrite and died upon that state, may his eye never find comfort.

The cause of this pledge, as mentioned by more than one scholar, was that the Prophet (ﷺ) summoned Khirash ibn Umayyah al-Khuza'i and sent him to the Quraysh in Makkah, mounting him on his camel called al-Tha'lab, to convey to their nobles what he had come for, which was the 'umrah (lesser pilgrimage). This was when he (ﷺ) had halted at al-Hudaybiyyah. They hamstrung the camel of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and wanted to kill him, but the Ahabish protected him. The Ahabish (*al-Ahabish*) are groups of various tribes, whose singular is *Ahbush*. Today they are called *al-lafif al-ajnabi* (the foreign legion), a term for an army whose members come from various countries and states. They let him go until he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Here the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Umar ibn al-Khattab to send him to Makkah to convey to the nobles of the Quraysh what he had come for. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I fear the Quraysh for myself, and there is no one in Makkah from the Banu 'Adi ibn Ka'b who would protect me, and the Quraysh know my enmity toward them and my harshness against them. But I will direct you to a man who is more honored among them than I am: 'Uthman ibn 'Affan." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned 'Uthman and sent him to Abu Sufyan and the nobles of the Quraysh to inform them that he had not come for war, but had come only as a visitor to this House, venerating its sanctity. 'Uthman went to Makkah, and Aban ibn Sa'id ibn al-'As met him when he entered Makkah, or before he entered it. He dismounted from his mount, carried him before himself, then rode behind him, and gave him protection until he conveyed the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). 'Uthman then went to Abu Sufyan and the leaders of the Quraysh and conveyed to them what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had sent him with. When he finished the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they said to 'Uthman: "If you wish to circumambulate the House, then circumambulate it." He said: "I would not do so until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) circumambulates it." So the Quraysh detained him. Then word reached the Messenger of Allah and the Muslims that 'Uthman had been killed.

At that, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We will not depart until we engage these people," and he called the people to pledge allegiance. Thus was the Pledge of Ridwan under the tree. This is the meaning of the words of the Exalted: *"Indeed Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree, and He knew what was in their hearts"*, that is, of truthfulness and loyalty. *"So He sent down tranquility upon them"*, that is, calm and steadfastness. *"And rewarded them"*, that is, recompensed them for their truthfulness and loyalty, *"with a near victory"*, which is the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyyah and the conquest of Khaybar. *"And much booty that they will take"*, which is the spoils of Khaybar. *"And Allah is ever Exalted in Might"*, that is, dominant over His command, *"Wise"* in His arrangement for His allies.

**Guidance from the two verses:**

1. Demonstration of the virtue of the people of the Pledge of Ridwan, and Allah's honoring of them by His pleasure with them.

2. The intelligence of Umar and the strength of his insight, when he ordered the tree to be cut down out of fear that it would be worshipped. How many trees have been worshipped in the nation of Islam in the absence of the scholars and the people of the Qur'an.

3. Allah the Exalted's reward to the truthful, patient, and striving servants among the believers, with the good of this world and the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 48, verses 20–24:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Wa'adakumu Allahu maghanima kathiratan ta'khudhunaha﴾ (God promised you many spoils that you will take): i.e., from the Islamic conquests that reached al-Andalus in the west.

﴿Fa'ajjala lakum hadhihi﴾ (So He hastened this for you): i.e., the spoils of Khaybar.

﴿Wa kafa aydiya al-nas 'ankum﴾ (And He restrained the hands of people from you): i.e., the hands of the Jews, who had resolved to raid the homes of the Companions, where their wives, children and property were, so God turned them away from them.

﴿Wa litakuna ayatan lil-mu'minin﴾ (And that it might be a sign for the believers): i.e., that turning away by which God diverted the hearts of the plotting Jews from attacking the families of the Companions, while they were absent at al-Hudaybiyah or Khaybar, is a sign by which they derive evidence of God's protection and safeguarding of them, whether present or absent.

﴿Wa yahdikum siratan mustaqiman﴾ (And guide you to a straight path): i.e., a path of trust in God and entrusting oneself to Him, whether present or absent, with no crookedness in it.

﴿Wa ukhra lam taqdiru 'alayha﴾ (And another [spoils] you were not able to obtain): i.e., and other spoils you were not able to obtain, namely the spoils of Persia and Byzantium (al-Rum).

﴿Qad ahata biha﴾ (God has encompassed them): i.e., they are guarded for you until you raid Persia and Byzantium and take them.

﴿Wa law qatalakumu alladhina kafaru﴾ (And if those who disbelieved fought you): i.e., the polytheists at al-Hudaybiyah.

﴿Lawallu al-adbar﴾ (They would have turned their backs): i.e., they would have been routed before you, giving you their backs to strike.

﴿Sunnata Allahi allati qad khalat min qabl﴾ (The way of God that has already passed before): i.e., the defeat of the disbelievers and the victory of the patient believers is an established way of God, in every time and place.

﴿Wa huwa alladhi kaffa aydiyahum 'ankum﴾ (And it is He who restrained their hands from you): when eighty men of the polytheists came intending to reach the Messenger of God and the believers to harm them.

﴿Wa aydiyakum 'anhum bi-batni Makkah﴾ (And your hands from them in the valley of Makkah): so the Companions of the Messenger of God took them captive and brought them to the Messenger of God, and he pardoned them.

﴿Min ba'di an azfarakum 'alayhim﴾ (After He had given you victory over them): this was at al-Hudaybiyah, which is in the valley of Makkah.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to speak of God's bounty and favour upon the believers who pledged allegiance to God and His Messenger to engage and fight the polytheists and not to flee. He mentioned that He sent down tranquillity upon them, rewarded them with a near victory and the many spoils of Khaybar. He then joined to the previous a further great report, saying: ﴿God promised you many spoils that you will take, and He hastened this for you﴾, i.e., the spoils of Khaybar, ﴿and restrained the hands of people from you﴾. This was because the Jews of Madinah conspired with the Jews of Khaybar and some Arabs to raid the homes of the Ansar and the Muhajirun in Madinah, to kill those within and plunder what was there; so the Most High restrained their hands and turned them away from what they intended, as an honour to the believers. His saying ﴿And that it might be a sign for the believers﴾ means: that turning away, by which He diverted the hearts of those who had intended to raid the families and households of the Companions in Madinah while they were absent at al-Hudaybiyah, is a sign guiding them to increase their trust in God, entrusting themselves to Him and relying upon Him. His saying ﴿And guide you to a straight path﴾ means: and He will make you firm on a clear path with no crookedness, which is that you trust your Lord in all your affairs, so you rely upon Him in all of them, and He will suffice you in all that concerns you and ward off from you what harms you, whether in your absence or your presence. His saying, the Exalted, ﴿And other [spoils] you were not able to obtain, God has encompassed them﴾ means: and other spoils you were not able to obtain, namely the spoils of Byzantium and Persia. God has encompassed them, so nothing of them will escape until you raid those lands and take them in full. ﴿And ever is God over all things competent﴾: among the manifestations of His power is that He grants you spoils while you are fewer in number and equipment, the spoils of the two greatest powers of that time, Persia and Byzantium.

His saying ﴿And if those who disbelieved fought you, they would have turned their backs; then they would not find any protector or helper﴾ means: and among the sum of His favours upon you is that if the people of Makkah had fought you while you were in its valley, God would have given you victory over them, and they would have fled before you, turning their backs, and they would find no protector to defend them nor helper to aid them, because We empowered you over them. His saying, the Exalted, ﴿The way of God that has already passed before﴾ means: among the earlier nations, namely that God surely supports His allies against His enemies. This is like the cosmic laws that do not change, and this is the meaning of His saying ﴿and you will not find any change in the way of God﴾. His saying in the last verse of this context [24] ﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Makkah after He had given you victory over them. And ever is God, of what you do, Seeing﴾ is another favour and a great honour: Quraysh sent eighty young men toward the army of the Messenger of God at al-Hudaybiyah, perhaps to catch the Messenger and his Companions unaware and strike them with harm; so the Most High caused them to fall as captives in the hands of the Muslims, and the Messenger ﷺ pardoned them, and this was the cause of the treaty of al-Hudaybiyah. His saying ﴿And ever is God, of what you do, Seeing﴾ means: Knowing and Aware of everything that occurs among you; He is with you through His guardianship over you.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The truth of God's promise to the Companions of His Messenger regarding the spoils they were promised; His words were fulfilled after the death of the Messenger of God ﷺ, namely the spoils of Persia and Byzantium.

2- God's honour toward the believers, for He protected their backs from behind twice: the first was what the Jews intended of a raid on the families and households of the Companions in the Prophet's city; the second was what men of the polytheists intended, to surprise the believers by night at al-Hudaybiyah, when God empowered His Messenger and the believers over them; then the Messenger of God pardoned them and released them, and that was a strong aid toward achieving the treaty of al-Hudaybiyah.

3- Clarification of God's way: that no fight between the allies of God and His enemies in a battle occurs except that God grants His allies victory over their enemies.

﴿And the offering detained from reaching its place﴾: i.e., and they prevented the offering from reaching its place of sacrifice in the Sacred Precinct while it was detained.

﴿And if not for believing men and believing women﴾: i.e., present in Makkah.

﴿You did not know them﴾: i.e., you did not know them to be believers, men and women.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 48, verses 27–28:

Explanation of the words:

"Indeed Allah has fulfilled the vision of His Messenger in truth": that is, Allah made the vision His Messenger saw in sleep during the year of al-Hudaybiyyah come true.

"You will surely enter al-Masjid al-Haram, if Allah wills, in security": this is the content of the vision, meaning: you will surely enter al-Masjid al-Haram, if Allah wills, in security.

"With your heads shaved and hair cut short": that is, shaving all your hair or cutting it short.

"Fearing no one": that is, at no time, during the state of ihram and after it.

"He knew what you did not know": that is, regarding the treaty that was concluded. That is, you did not know of the harm that would have befallen the Muslims by fighting their brothers in faith while they were unaware.

"So He made, besides that, a near victory": this is the conquest of Khaybar, and the vision was realized in the following year.

"He it is who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth": therefore He does not fail to fulfill his vision, but confirms it.

"To make it prevail over all religion": that is, to elevate it above all other religions by abrogating the truth in them and nullifying the falsehood in them, or by empowering the Muslims over their adherents so that they rule over them.

"And sufficient is Allah as Witness": that is, you are a messenger with what was mentioned, namely the guidance and the religion of truth.

The meaning of the verses:

The context remains on the treaty of al-Hudaybiyyah and the events that took place in it. Allah the Exalted said, "Indeed Allah has fulfilled the vision of His Messenger" — that is, Muhammad (ﷺ) — "in truth": that is, the vision that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw and told his Companions about when they set out from Madinah to Makkah. He informed his Companions of it, and they rejoiced and were delighted. When the treaty was concluded after a grueling political and military struggle, and the Messenger ordered them to sacrifice and shave, they were astonished, and some of them said, "Where is the vision you saw?" Surat al-Fath was revealed when they returned from al-Hudaybiyyah, and in it is the saying of Allah the Exalted: "You will surely enter al-Masjid al-Haram, if Allah wills, in security, with your heads shaved and hair cut short, fearing no one." Allah had indeed fulfilled His Messenger's vision in truth. When the following year came, in the same days of the month of Dhu al-Qa'dah, the Messenger of Allah and the Muslims set out in the state of ihram, reciting the talbiyah, and Quraysh vacated al-Masjid al-Haram for them. They circumambulated the House, performed sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and exited their 'umrah, some shaving and some cutting short.

As for His saying, "So He knew what you did not know," it affirms and establishes the treaty, because had there been fighting and no treaty, the believing men in Makkah and the believing women would have been destroyed by war, and a great harm would have befallen the Muslims who killed their brothers in Islam. This is among the matters that required the treaty and the abandoning of fighting. As for His saying, "And He made, besides that, a near victory," the treaty is a victory, the conquest of Khaybar is a victory, and the conquest of Makkah is a victory; all of them are near victory. As for His saying, "He it is who sent His Messenger," that is, Muhammad, "with guidance and the religion of truth," that is, Islam, how then would He not confirm his vision, as some have supposed? "And sufficient is Allah as Witness" that you, O Muhammad, are a messenger with what Allah the Exalted mentioned: the guidance and the religion of truth, and its prevalence over all religion by abrogating the truth in other religions and nullifying the falsehood attached to them, or by empowering the Muslims to subdue and rule the people of those false religions. Something great has already come of this.

Guidance from the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- Affirmation that the visions of the prophets are true.

2- The interpretation of a vision may be delayed for a year or more.

3- The legitimacy of shaving and cutting the hair to exit from Hajj or 'Umrah, and that shaving is better because it is mentioned first.

4- The legitimacy of saying "if Allah wills" in every statement or action that refers to the future.

5- Islam is the religion of truth, and whatever is other than it is falsehood.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 48, verse 29:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him⦈: that is, his Companions, may Allah be pleased with them.

﴿Severe against the disbelievers⦈: that is, harsh, showing them no mercy.

﴿Merciful among themselves⦈: that is, compassionate and affectionate toward one another, like a father with his child.

﴿You see them bowing and prostrating⦈: that is, you see them bowing and prostrating, i.e., performing ruku' and sujud.

﴿Seeking bounty from Allah and His pleasure⦈: that is, they seek through their bowing and prostration a reward from their Lord, which is Paradise, and "pleasure," which is His approval, Mighty and Majestic is He.

﴿Their mark is on their faces⦈: that is, a light and whiteness by which they will be recognized on the Day of Resurrection as having prostrated in this world.

﴿That⦈: that is, the described attribute.

﴿Their likeness in the Torah⦈: that is, their description in the Torah, the Book of Moses, peace be upon him.

﴿Its shoot⦈: that is, its offshoots.

﴿Then strengthens it⦈: that is, strengthens it and helps it.

﴿Then it becomes thick⦈ and ﴿stands firm⦈: that is, it becomes thick and stands firm, i.e., grows strong.

﴿On its stalk⦈: plural of saq, meaning on its roots.

﴿Pleasing the sowers⦈: that is, pleasing those who sow it, because of its beauty.

﴿That He may enrage the disbelievers by them⦈: this is a reason: that is, He strengthened them and increased them so that He might enrage the disbelievers by them.

The meaning of the verses:

When Allah, exalted is He, informed that He sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religion, as a testimony from Him to that, He also informed about him something that confirms that testimony, saying: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him⦈, from among his Companions, ﴿are severe against the disbelievers⦈, that is, harsh and hard upon them. This is for two reasons. The first is that they disbelieved in Allah, opposed Him, did not believe in Him, and did not respond to Him, and Allah hates them for that; so they are harsh toward them for that reason. The second is that harshness and severity may be a cause of their guidance, because they are pained by it, and they see its opposite with the Muslims, so they embrace Islam, and then they receive mercy and succeed. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿merciful among themselves⦈, that is, among themselves they show compassion and mercy to one another. So you see one of them disliking that the body or garment of a disbeliever touch his body or garment, and you see him with a Muslim: when he sees him he shakes his hand, embraces him, is gentle with him, helps him, and shows him love and affection. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿You see them⦈, that is, you, the addressee, see them ﴿bowing and prostrating⦈, that is, bowing and prostrating in their prayers. ﴿Seeking⦈, that is, they seek through their prayer, after their faith and their mutual cooperation, love and compassion for one another, they seek by that ﴿bounty from Allah and pleasure⦈, that is, Paradise and the pleasure of Allah. This is the loftiest thing a believer can seek: that Allah admit him into Paradise after rescuing him from the Fire, and be pleased with him. His saying ﴿Their mark is on their faces, from the trace of prostration⦈, that is, the signs of their faith and purity are on their faces from the trace of prostration, for they will be raised on the Day of Resurrection with bright faces and white limbs from the traces of ablution, ﴿their light running before them and on their right⦈ [al-Tahrim: 8]. And in this world, upon them are the marks of piety, righteousness, humility, gentleness and mercy. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿That⦈, that is, the mentioned description, ﴿is their likeness in the Torah⦈ ﴿and their likeness in the Gospel is like a seed that sends forth its shoot⦈, that is, its offshoots, ﴿then strengthens it⦈, that is, strengthens it and helps it, ﴿then it becomes thick⦈, that is, becomes thick, ﴿then stands firm⦈, that is, grows strong, ﴿on its stalk⦈, the stalk being that from its root which bears the ear of grain, ﴿pleasing the sowers⦈, that is, those who sow it, because of its beauty and the soundness of its produce. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿that He may enrage the disbelievers by them⦈, that is, He strengthened them and increased them so that He might enrage the disbelievers by them. For this reason it is related from Malik ibn Anas, may Allah have mercy on him, that whoever is enraged by the Companions of the Messenger of Allah is a disbeliever. His saying ﴿Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds among them forgiveness⦈, that is, for their sins, ﴿and a great reward⦈, which is Paradise.

This is a promise specific to the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, may Allah be pleased with them. There is also a general promise for all believing men and women, found in other verses, such as the verse of al-Ma'idah: ﴿Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds: for them is forgiveness and a great reward⦈ [al-Ma'idah: 9].

Guidance from the noble verse:

Among the guidance of the noble verse:

1- Affirmation of the prophethood of the Messenger of Allah and confirmation of his mission.

2- A statement of what the Messenger of Allah and his Companions were upon: severity and harshness toward the disbelievers, and compassion and mercy toward the people of faith. This is something it is obligatory to follow them in and to emulate.

3- A statement of the virtue of prayer with bowing, prostration, tranquility and humility.

4- The description of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah in both the Torah and the Gospel raises their rank and elevates their station.

5- A statement that the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began few and then kept increasing until they became numerous to a degree that enraged the disbelievers.

6- Hatred toward the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is completely incompatible with faith, especially toward their best and senior ones, such as the four Rightly Guided Caliphs, the ten promised Paradise, the people of the Pledge of al-Ridwan, and before them the people of Badr. For this reason it is related from Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, that whoever is enraged by the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is a disbeliever.
